cues: The essay opens with Croesus, the ancient king of Lydia, so rich that his name became a proverb.
Imagine a modern Croesus: fabulously wealthy, but kind.
He hates cruelty and insists that nobody in his kingdom starve.
A world where one man owns everything and treats everyone decently is still a world of extreme inequality.
And that, he says, is our world: human rights fight repression and misery, but sit comfortably beside enormous wealth.
text: The essay opens with Croesus, the ancient king of Lydia, so rich that his name became a proverb. Imagine a modern Croesus: fabulously wealthy, but kind. He hates cruelty and insists that nobody in his kingdom starve. Who could object? Moyn can. A world where one man owns everything and treats everyone decently is still a world of extreme inequality. And that, he says, is our world: human rights fight repression and misery, but sit comfortably beside enormous wealth.
